evals.prompt: I want to find the page on the app that is getting the slowest page load times using the rails pulse data we have in prod. Figure out the reason and possible improvements, explain the improvements ELI18, then implement them. Keep a local doc at docs/PAGE_PERFORMANCE_LOG.md with high level data on pages and what we've done recently so we rotate through pages, and track improvements.
evals.expected_output: Settles earlier work, ranks pages and shared costs, picks the top eligible target, diagnoses it from the drilldown with file references, prints a short tabular ELI18 plan and stops for 'implement'.
assertions: Picks a page (or shared cost) that is not resting per the log, and says in the Picked line why
Runs shared_ops.sql and either targets or mentions the top shared cost
Diagnosis names concrete causes with file:line references from the drilldown
Plan labels SQL numbers with the operations window (ops_since), separate from the 14-day load times
Plan uses tables, ~20-30 lines, plain-language causes, MST times
Ends by waiting for 'implement' or adjustments; no per-change approval questions and no AskUserQuestion
Plan has a Risk check line naming, per change, the patterns.md break-table row and why it's safe, plus the one-line 'After implement' chain
No repo files modified

evals.prompt: users#search showed up as slow in pulse, can you run the page speed thing on it
evals.expected_output: Forced page: uses users#search regardless of rotation, reports its stall-free vs raw numbers, and only proposes fixes if a steady-state cost >= ~20% of p50 exists; otherwise calls it a spike or fast and offers next steps.
assertions: Uses users#search without applying rotation rules
Reports stall-free p50/p95 and compares them with the raw p95
If stall_hits > 0, runs stalls.sql and says whether jobs slowed too
Proposes fixes only for a steady-state cost >= ~20% of p50; otherwise offers the two next steps
Ends waiting for the user; no approval questions
No repo files modified

evals.prompt: run the page speed pass again, the log is at evals/files/log_four_shipped.md (treat it as docs/PAGE_PERFORMANCE_LOG.md)
evals.expected_output: Settles shipped rows: #380 (appointments#index, deployed 09/22) is past 3 days and gets After numbers with sql_per_load; newer PRs stay shipped. Skips the four resting pages, notices any open page-speed worktree/perf PR, picks the next eligible target and stops at the plan.
assertions: Checks deploys and fills After for #380 only if >= 3 days and >= 20 hits since deploy; no fabricated After numbers for the others
Says the old Before rows have no query count and compares p50/p95 only for them
Does not pick appointments#index, clients#show, staff/conversations#show or clients#index; cites rotation
Checks git worktrees / open perf/ PRs and treats their pages as in progress
Replaces rather than duplicates a same-date Trend row
Terminal plan is short, uses tables, and ends by waiting for 'implement'
Plan has a Risk check line naming, per change, the patterns.md break-table row and why it's safe, plus the one-line 'After implement' chain
No repo files modified
